title: The M. tuberculosis complex
dek: MTBC is a clonal pack of host-adapted ecotypes, not a species label you can treat as DST. RD deletions and SNPs do the speciation; Xpert does not.
story: The Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) is a set of ecotypes that share >99.9% nucleotide identity and a clonal, almost plasmid-free, population structure. Human-adapted members are M. tuberculosis sensu stricto (lineages L1–L4, L7, L8) and M. africanum (L5, L6, plus L9 in current schemes). Animal-adapted members include M. bovis, M. caprae, M. microti, M. pinnipedii, M. orygis, M. suricattae, M. mungi. M. canettii sits just outside the clonal MTBC as a smooth, putative ancestral-like taxon.

Most NAATs, including Xpert, answer “MTBC nucleic acid present.” They do not name the ecotype. That is a speciation problem, not a cartridge failure: a BCG bladder-instillation isolate, a M. bovis from unpasteurised dairy, and an L2 Beijing pulmonary strain all light the same MTBC lamp.

Region-of-difference (RD) deletions and a small SNP barcode do the actual naming. RD1 is gone in BCG. RD9 is gone in M. africanum and animal-adapted lineages. M. bovis carries a characteristic pncA H57D (or lineage-defining equivalent) that makes PZA intrinsic-R. Lineage is a covariate for mutation rate, PE/PPE content, and sometimes resistance priors — it is not a drug.
deepTitle: What a genomics lab actually calls
deep: Coll’s 62-SNP barcode (and later expansions) assigns L1–L7 stably; L8 and L9 are rare African lineages added as sampling improved. L2/Beijing is over-represented in many MDR datasets. That is epidemiology plus maybe a slightly higher mutation supply, not a licence to call BDQ-R from lineage alone.

M. canettii is the exception that teaches the rule: it recombines, has a larger accessory genome, and is not a typical pulmonary-TB outbreak organism. Do not force-fit a canettii assembly into an H37Rv-only DST pipeline without looking at the tree.

M. bovis BCG used as a cancer therapy is a recurring “RR-TB” false alarm when someone sequences a urine isolate, sees MTBC, and then over-reads pncA. RD1 deletion plus BCG-specific SNPs close the case.

MAC (M. avium complex) and other NTM are not MTBC. A mis-speciated MGIT bottle will happily generate a “pan-susceptible TB” report for an organism that does not live in the catalogue. Kraken/Mykrobe species calls belong in the same report as rpoB.

visual.caption: MTBC nested under Mycobacterium. Human-adapted lineages are the usual pulmonary-TB object. Animal-adapted leaves share the NAAT target and not the PZA story.

example.title: Urine MTBC that is BCG
example.setup: Oncology patient, BCG instillations, urine Xpert MTB/RIF positive, RIF not detected. WGS: M. bovis BCG, RD1 deleted, pncA BCG allele.

steps.title: Do not start 2HRZE
steps.body: This is not airborne DS-TB until proven otherwise. The NAAT is working; the species question was never asked.

steps.title: PZA is not acquired MDR
steps.body: Intrinsic pncA in M. bovis/BCG is not a treatment-emergent mutation. Reporting it as acquired PZA-R contaminates surveillance.

steps.title: Name the ecotype
steps.body: RD1 deletion plus BCG SNP barcode is the result. Then call the oncologist, not the MDR ward.

example.takeaway: MTBC-positive is a door, not a species or a regimen.

check.prompt: Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra reports MTB detected. Which statement is true?
choices: The isolate is M. tuberculosis sensu stricto lineage 4
MTBC nucleic acid is present; ecotype (Mtb vs bovis/BCG vs africanum) is not resolved
NTM have been excluded at species level
check.answer: MTBC nucleic acid is present; ecotype (Mtb vs bovis/BCG vs africanum) is not resolved
check.why: The cartridge target is MTBC DNA plus an rpoB window. Speciation is a different assay.

whyWrong.The isolate is M. tuberculosis sensu str: Lineage is not an Xpert output.
whyWrong.NTM have been excluded at species level: Most NTM should not trigger MTB detected, but the positive call is still not a full species ID among MTBC.

check.prompt: RD9 is deleted in M. africanum and animal-adapted MTBC, present in M. tuberculosis sensu stricto. An isolate with RD9 present and RD1 present is most consistent with:
check.why: BCG lacks RD1. M. bovis lacks RD9. M. avium is not MTBC.

check.prompt: On the hierarchy plate, why do M. bovis and BCG sit on a different row from L1–L4?
choices: Because they are animal-adapted / vaccine ecotypes inside MTBC, not the usual human-adapted pulmonary lineages
check.answer: Because they are animal-adapted / vaccine ecotypes inside MTBC, not the usual human-adapted pulmonary lineages
check.why: The plate is an ecotype tree, not a NAAT tree. BCG is still MTBC.
